title: What someone said
verifiedBy: LLM review, authorised by repo owner

allowedTenses: passato prossimo — the reporting verb (ha detto, ha chiesto)
imperfetto — the backshifted clause, L2-M10's tense in a second seat

rules.text: REPORTING MOVES THE TENSE BACK ONE STEP, AND ITALIAN'S STEP IS THE IMPERFETTO. Dice che è stanco becomes Ha detto che era stanco; dice che vuole tornare becomes Ha detto che voleva tornare. English does exactly the same thing — "he says he is" becomes "he said he was" — so the move itself is free. The only new part is which past Italian reaches for, and it is L2-M10's, doing a second job here rather than a new one.

A YES/NO QUESTION IS REPORTED WITH SE, NEVER WITH CHE. Mi ha chiesto SE avevo tempo — never mi ha chiesto che avevo tempo. English pours "that" after every verb of saying and then quietly switches to "if" for a question, so the switch is invisible to a learner and the wrong word arrives by habit. A wh-question keeps its own word instead: mi ha chiesto DOVE lavoravo, mi ha chiesto QUANDO tornavo. Same se as L3-M4's, different job.

A REQUEST IS NOT A CLAUSE AT ALL: it becomes di plus an infinitive. Mi ha detto DI aspettare, mi ha chiesto DI richiamare. English keeps a person in it — "he told me to wait" — and Italian does not need one after the mi. This is the same di as L1-M9's penso di and L3-M3's escape hatch, doing the job it always does: gluing an infinitive to the verb in front of it.

THE OBJECT CLITICS ARE SPELLED EXACTLY LIKE THE ARTICLES, so this course never teaches them bare. la and le have been L1-M1's articles since the first rung and they stay that way; the object words are taught welded to the verb they lean on — l'ho vista, li ho visti, le ho parlato, ne ho — one key each, with the elision inside it and a straight apostrophe. It is the same tool as a destra and più tardi, and it is why a learner is never asked to tell two identical words apart on sight.

THE PARTICIPLE AGREES WITH A PRECEDING DIRECT-OBJECT CLITIC AND WITH NOTHING ELSE ON AVERE. L'ho vista (a woman), li ho visti (them) — but Ho visto Anna, with no agreement at all, because the object comes AFTER. And le ho parlato never agrees whoever le is, because le is indirect: you speak TO her. The limit matters as much as the rule; a learner who takes the pattern as "participles agree" will bend every one in the account, and L1-M5's essere agreement is a separate law with its own reason.

NE IS A WORD ENGLISH DOES NOT HAVE. Ne ho due is "I have two OF THEM", and the of-them is compulsory in Italian where English simply drops it — "I have two" on its own is not sayable here. It leans on the verb like the other clitics and it is taught the same way, welded to it.

sentences.display: Ha detto che era molto stanco
sentences.cue: He said he was very tired
sentences.literal: He-has said that he-was very tired

words.note: The participle of dire, irregular and short — never dicuto. Ha detto is the whole reporting verb, and what follows it steps back a tense.

sentences.trap: The step back is free, because English takes it too — "he said he was", not "he said he is". What is not free is which past: Italian takes the imperfetto here and never the passato prossimo, so ha detto che è stato stanco says something else entirely.
sentences.sound: a DET-to ke E-ra. The double t of detto is held, and era is stressed on its first syllable.

variations.display: Ha detto che era contento
variations.cue: He said he was happy

variations.display: Ha detto che aveva un problema
variations.cue: He said he had a problem

variations.display: Mi ha detto che era stanco
variations.cue: He told me he was tired

mistake.display: Ha detto che è molto stanco
mistake.why: Reporting steps the clause back: Ha detto che era molto stanco.

sentences.usage: The opening line of every account of a conversation you were in.

sentences.display: Mi ha detto che voleva tornare a casa
sentences.cue: He told me he wanted to go home
sentences.literal: To-me he-has said that he-wanted to-return at home

words.note: The imperfetto of voglio, vuoi and vuole, and what dice che vuole becomes once ha detto stands in front of it. It still takes a bare infinitive.

sentences.trap: mi here is the person told, not a reflexive: mi ha detto is "he told ME". L3-M1's mi alzo points a verb back at its own subject and this mi points it at somebody else — one family of little words, two jobs, exactly as L3-M1's rule warned.
sentences.sound: mee a DET-to ke vo-LE-va. voleva is stressed on the LE, and the whole thing runs as one phrase.

variations.display: Mi ha detto che voleva restare
variations.cue: He told me he wanted to stay

variations.display: Ha detto che voleva parlare con il capo
variations.cue: He said he wanted to talk to the boss
variations.changed: no mi, so nobody is told in particular

variations.display: Mi ha detto che andava a Roma
variations.cue: He told me he was going to Rome

mistake.display: Mi ha detto che voleva di tornare a casa
mistake.why: volere takes the bare infinitive in any tense: Mi ha detto che voleva tornare a casa.

sentences.usage: Passing on what somebody told you, with the person they told left in.
sentences.mnemonic: vuole → voleva. Same verb, one step back.

sentences.display: Mi ha chiesto se avevo tempo
sentences.cue: She asked me if I had time
sentences.literal: To-me she-has asked if I-had time

words.note: The participle of chiedere, and it keeps nothing of the infinitive's look. Ha chiesto is asked a QUESTION; ha detto di is asked FOR something.

sentences.trap: English says "asked me if" and then says "told me that", and a learner carries the that across into the question: mi ha chiesto che avevo tempo is the commonest wrong sentence in this module. A reported yes/no question takes se and nothing else.
sentences.sound: mee a KYES-to se a-VE-vo. chiesto opens with a ky, not a ch as in church.

variations.display: Mi ha chiesto se avevo i soldi
variations.cue: She asked me if I had the money

variations.display: Mi ha chiesto se ero stanco
variations.cue: She asked me if I was tired

variations.display: Mi ha chiesto se lavoravo oggi
variations.cue: She asked me if I was working today
variations.changed: a verb rather than a state

mistake.display: Mi ha chiesto che avevo tempo
mistake.why: A reported yes/no question takes se: Mi ha chiesto se avevo tempo.

sentences.usage: Reporting the question somebody put to you, which is half of any account of a call.

sentences.display: Mi ha chiesto dove lavoravo e quando tornavo
sentences.cue: She asked me where I worked and when I was coming back
sentences.literal: To-me she-has asked where I-worked and when I-returned

words.note: The imperfetto of L1-M10's torno, built exactly as L2-M10's lavoravo is. Nothing new happens to it in a reported question — it is the ordinary backshift.

sentences.trap: A wh-question keeps its own word and does not take se. dove stays dove and quando stays quando; only a yes/no question needs the se, and mixing the two is the other half of S03's error.
sentences.sound: DO-ve la-vo-RA-vo e KWAN-do tor-NA-vo. The two imperfetto verbs rhyme, which is the point.

variations.display: Mi ha chiesto dove lavoravo
variations.cue: She asked me where I worked

variations.display: Mi ha chiesto quando tornavo
variations.cue: She asked me when I was coming back

variations.display: Mi ha chiesto quando tornava mia sorella
variations.cue: She asked me when my sister was coming back

mistake.display: Mi ha chiesto se dove lavoravo
mistake.why: A wh-word replaces the se, it does not join it: Mi ha chiesto dove lavoravo.

sentences.usage: Reporting the two questions a stranger always asks, in one line.
sentences.mnemonic: se for yes/no. dove and quando for the rest.

sentences.display: Mi ha detto di aspettare qui
sentences.cue: He told me to wait here
sentences.literal: To-me he-has said of to-wait here

words.note: It swallows English's "for": aspettare l'autobus, never aspettare per. The verb carries the whole meaning and needs no preposition after it.

sentences.trap: A reported request is not a clause. English builds "he told me TO wait" out of a person and an infinitive; Italian puts the person in the mi and then hangs the infinitive off di, with no che and no second subject anywhere.
sentences.sound: as-pet-TA-re. The double t is held and the stress sits on the TA.

variations.display: Mi ha detto di richiamare più tardi
variations.cue: He told me to call back later

variations.display: Mi ha detto di aspettare in ufficio
variations.cue: He told me to wait at the office

variations.display: Mi ha chiesto di aspettare
variations.cue: He asked me to wait
variations.changed: asked rather than told, and the same di

mistake.display: Mi ha detto che aspettare qui
mistake.why: A request takes di and an infinitive: Mi ha detto di aspettare qui.

sentences.usage: The message you pass on from a receptionist, a colleague or a friend.
sentences.mnemonic: Told to do → detto di + infinitive.

sentences.cue: I saw her yesterday at the office

words.note: ONE key with the elision inside it and a straight apostrophe. The l' underneath is the object her, not L1-M1's article la, which is why the phrase is taught whole and never split.

sentences.trap: The word for her is spelled la, exactly like the article a learner has been reading since L1-M1, and in front of ho it elides to l' so even the spelling disappears. That is why this course never asks you to recognise the bare word: the phrase is the unit.
sentences.sound: lo VEE-sta. l'ho is one syllable — the h is silent — so the whole thing is three beats, lo-VEE-sta.

variations.display: L'ho vista stamattina
variations.cue: I saw her this morning

variations.display: L'ho vista al bar con Anna
variations.cue: I saw her at the bar with Anna

variations.display: Non l'ho vista ieri
variations.cue: I didn't see her yesterday
variations.changed: negated, with the non in front of the whole thing

mistake.display: Ho visto la ieri in ufficio
mistake.why: The object leans on the verb in front of it: L'ho vista ieri in ufficio.

sentences.usage: The line that starts most gossip and most alibis.
sentences.mnemonic: l'ho vista — one word, not three.

sentences.display: Li ho visti al bar stamattina
sentences.cue: I saw them at the bar this morning
sentences.literal: Them I-have seen at-the bar this-morning

words.note: The plural of l'ho vista, and the participle moves with it: visti for them, vista for her. li is L2-M5's word doing the object job it always did.

sentences.trap: Both ends move at once. The clitic picks the people — l' for her, li for them — and the participle follows it, so vista and visti are not a choice made twice but one agreement made once, at the front of the phrase.
sentences.sound: lee o VEES-tee. No elision here: li keeps its i in front of ho, unlike la.

variations.display: Li ho visti al cinema
variations.cue: I saw them at the cinema

variations.display: Li ho visti ieri con i miei amici
variations.cue: I saw them yesterday with my friends

variations.display: Non li ho visti stamattina
variations.cue: I didn't see them this morning

mistake.display: Li ho visto al bar stamattina
mistake.why: The participle agrees with the clitic in front of it: Li ho visti al bar stamattina.

sentences.usage: Reporting a sighting of a group, and the plural half of the same rule.

sentences.display: Le ho parlato al telefono ieri
sentences.cue: I spoke to her on the phone yesterday
sentences.literal: To-her I-have spoken at-the telephone yesterday

words.note: The le here is TO her, not the plural article of L1-M1. It never elides in front of ho and the participle never agrees with it, because it is indirect.

sentences.trap: This is where the agreement rule stops. le is indirect — you speak TO somebody — so parlato stays parlato however many women are involved, and le ho parlata is wrong. Only a preceding DIRECT object moves the participle.
sentences.sound: le o par-LA-to. le keeps its e in front of ho: never l'ho parlato.

variations.display: Le ho parlato ieri
variations.cue: I spoke to her yesterday

variations.display: Le ho parlato in ufficio stamattina
variations.cue: I spoke to her at the office this morning

variations.display: Non le ho parlato oggi
variations.cue: I haven't spoken to her today

mistake.why: You speak TO somebody, so the clitic is le and nothing agrees: Le ho parlato al telefono ieri.

sentences.usage: The other half of an account of a phone call — who you spoke to, not who you saw.
sentences.mnemonic: Spoken TO her: le, and no agreement.

sentences.display: Vuoi i biglietti? Ne ho due
sentences.cue: Do you want the tickets? I've got two
sentences.literal: You-want the tickets? Of-them I-have two

words.note: ne is "of them" and English drops it. Ho due on its own is not a sentence in Italian: the ne is what the two are two OF, and it leans on the verb.

sentences.trap: English says "I've got two" and stops. Italian cannot: without the ne there is nothing for due to count, and Ho due lands as an unfinished sentence a listener waits for the end of.
sentences.sound: ne o DOO-e. ne ho is two quick beats — the h is silent — and due is fully two syllables.

variations.display: Ne ho due
variations.cue: I've got two of them

variations.display: Vuoi i biglietti? Ne ho tre
variations.cue: Do you want the tickets? I've got three

variations.display: Ne ho due, ma sono vecchi
variations.cue: I've got two of them, but they're old

mistake.why: A counted thing needs its ne: Vuoi i biglietti? Ne ho due.

sentences.usage: Answering how many you have of something already named, which is what ne is for.
sentences.mnemonic: ne = of them, and it is never dropped.

sentences.display: Ho visto Anna ieri, e l'ho vista anche oggi
sentences.cue: I saw Anna yesterday, and I saw her today too
sentences.literal: I-have seen Anna yesterday, and her-I-have seen also today

words.note: The plain participle of vedere, and the shape it keeps whenever the object comes after it: ho visto Anna, ho visto i miei amici. Nothing agrees.

sentences.trap: One sentence, both halves of the law. The object after the verb leaves the participle alone — ho visto Anna — and the same object in front of it as a clitic moves it — l'ho vista. Position is the whole rule, and it is the half a learner drops first.
sentences.sound: o VEES-to AN-na. visto and vista differ only in the last vowel, and that vowel is doing all the grammar.

variations.display: Ho visto Anna al bar
variations.cue: I saw Anna at the bar

variations.display: L'ho vista anche oggi
variations.cue: I saw her today too

variations.display: Ho visto i miei amici ieri
variations.cue: I saw my friends yesterday
variations.changed: a plural object, still after the verb, still visto

mistake.display: Ho vista Anna ieri, e l'ho visto anche oggi
mistake.why: Both halves are the wrong way round: Ho visto Anna ieri, e l'ho vista anche oggi.

sentences.usage: The module's whole rule said once, in a sentence somebody would actually say.
sentences.mnemonic: Object after: visto. Object in front: vista.
